pointers.needs: The shared anchors this volume relies on, declared as needs until shared/ lands

shared-needs.rule: shared/ belongs to the shared author (brief C, "What R-03 produces"); this volume never writes it and never points into it before it exists. Each need names the volume and the anchor the shared author declares. check.sh (N-46) resolves a need by volume and anchor once the shared volume lands, so a need becomes a live pointer without a hand edit. The same needs are returned to the shared author as data by the seat that wrote this volume.
shared-needs.need: Rows for lease.recovered 100; lease.renewed 200; lease.granted 201; lease.released 204; lease.stale 412; lease.refused 423 (held, hold) and 429 (cap); lease.expired 500; lease.failed 500; break.glass (owner-only record kind). Owner-acts: lease.failed at three in ten minutes on one key.

leases(key PRIMARY KEY ticket:phase:attempt, ticket, phase, attempt, holder, token, generation, granted_at, expires_at, heartbeat_at, released_at, version); the token counter is entity counter:lease_token.
The store-wide fencing token only grows; N-01 refuses a Put whose token is not current for the record's ticket and attempt (412).
Two seats can never both act on one ticket phase; a silent seat loses its lease by time.
Liveness is a timestamp and the process table, never a pane read or a model opinion (V08, K04).
The launcher exports the token into the run; every seat Put carries it; the seat cannot claim, renew or release.

The launcher (N-15), not the model, renews every lease.heartbeat_seconds 30; the lease.ttl_seconds 900 leaves room for a service restart; N-12 finds a dead launcher at 3 missed beats (90 s); every node reads the same keys.
lease.ttl_seconds 900, lease.heartbeat_seconds 30, lease.caps (global jobs.in_flight 4 plus per-role), lease.keep_days 30, stall.tick_seconds 15; a missing key is exit 3 naming the key.
A lease past expires_at with no renewal: swept, generation bumped, lease.expired 500; N-12 kills the run, N-11 decides attempt n+1.

purpose.is: N-02 turns a claimable unit of work (a ticket at a phase and an attempt) into exactly one lease: one holder, one fencing token that only grows, one expiry, one generation. Every write the holder makes carries the token, and the store (N-01) refuses a stale one.
It is the collision answer of the whole factory: two seats can never both act on one ticket phase, and a seat that went silent loses its lease by time, never by opinion.
purpose.is-not: It does not dispatch (N-07), does not kill a run (N-12), does not retry (N-11), and never asks a model whether a holder is alive (SPEC-16 l-llm, K04).
purpose.decisions: D01 (the Go service owns leases and heartbeats), D17 (one-shot seats plus a stall timer, C49), D02 (one-shot runs, C36), T06 (lease with heartbeat, generation counter, compare-and-swap, renewed at a third of its length, never stolen while liveness is unknown).

record.field: worker or reviewer on a ticket (the reviewer phase re-enters on gate.verdict green, dag.md section 4), spec on a cut-request key CR-<request id> that N-03 admitted from a ticket.request (role spec-author, no file claims), or gate for the code role N-07 performs in process. The merge phase is never leased: N-09 serialises merges on merge.lock.
1 to 3 (re-entry from N-11 with attempt n+1).
The role the phase needs, from the ticket.

also.from: the holder's heartbeat (N-15) through the ctl CLI
the holder's seat.result (N-15) or a merge record (N-09)

also.note: the sweep that expires silent leases

input.rule: A claim is keyed on ticket, phase and attempt. The same key claimed twice is one lease and one 423 lease.refused, never two leases.

record.field: The dispatch id N-07 will create, or the seat name once N-15 starts the run; the holder is a string the store does not interpret.
Fencing token: a store-wide counter that only grows; every later token for any key is larger. Carried on every Put by the holder.
Per-key counter: how many times this key has been granted (expiry and re-grant bump it).
lease.heartbeat_seconds (default 30): the holder renews at this interval; N-12 judges a launcher dead after 3 missed beats, long before the ttl.
held (a live holder exists), cap (role or global concurrency cap reached: 429 instead of 423), hold (the HOLD flag is set), phase (the ticket is not at this phase).
When the holder's lease ends, so the caller knows the bound of its wait.

output.record: The sweep found a lease past expires_at with no renewal; the key is free and generation is bumped; N-12 reads this to kill the run.
A heartbeat renewed the lease; expires_at moved.
The holder released on its result; the key is terminal for this attempt.
A renew or release carried a token that is not current; logged, nothing changed.

mechanism.component: Go package scheduler/internal/lease: Claim, Renew, Release, Sweep, Current. Pure arithmetic for expiry and heartbeat bounds; the clock is core.Clock; the store is N-01's Put with an entity write.

leases (key PRIMARY KEY, ticket, phase, attempt, holder, token, generation, granted_at, expires_at, heartbeat_at, released_at, version) in coq.db, owned by this node; the token counter is one row of the entities table (key counter:lease_token) bumped with compare-and-swap.

System jobs lease keys of the form node:N-xx:KEY with their own ttl (shared/state-store.xml#table-leases): node:N-07:leader is the scheduler leader lease, ttl 30 s renewed every 10 s, which N-07 holds so one tick goroutine dispatches (nodes/N-07/spec.xml#many-agents); the service-wide flock on STATE/run/service.lock (N-06) refuses a second service process outright, and the leader lease covers the overlap of a stopping and a starting process that the flock hand-over leaves.
lease.caps from scheduler/config/scheduler.json: a global cap (jobs.in_flight, 4 today) and a per-role cap table; a cap counts live leases by role. The cap values are data, never prose (K10).
mechanism.mermaid: stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> free free --> held: Claim (CAS: no live holder) token=next() held --> held: Renew (token matches) expires_at+=ttl held --> free: Sweep (now > expires_at) lease.expired 500, generation+1 held --> released: Release (token matches) lease.released 204 held --> held: Claim by another (lease.refused 423) released --> [*] free --> free: Claim under cap or HOLD (lease.refused 429 or 423)
mechanism.step: Claim: in one Put transaction, read the key; if a row exists with released_at null and expires_at after now, 423 held. Else count live leases by role and globally against caps; over means 429 cap. Else if flag:hold is set, 423 hold. Else token = CAS increment of counter:lease_token; write the lease row with expected_version equal to the row's current version (0 when absent); append lease.granted 201.

Renew: UPDATE WHERE key AND token = given AND released_at IS NULL; zero rows means 412 lease.stale (logged); else expires_at = now + ttl, heartbeat_at = now, lease.renewed 200. A renew after expiry but before the sweep ran is honoured only if the generation has not moved; otherwise 412.
Release: UPDATE WHERE key AND token = given; sets released_at; lease.released 204. The ticket's phase entity moves in the same transaction (N-03 reads it).

Sweep (every stall tick from N-06): SELECT keys WHERE released_at IS NULL AND expires_at < now; for each, in its own transaction, bump generation, clear holder, append lease.expired 500 with the last heartbeat_at. N-12 consumes lease.expired to kill the run; N-11 consumes the stall to decide attempt n+1.
Current(ticket, attempt) answers the store's fencing check in N-01 step 3: the token is current when the row for that key has that token and released_at is null and expires_at is after now.
mechanism.ttl: lease.ttl_seconds 900 (herdr/config/leases.json#seat ttl 900, kept); the seat launcher (N-15) heartbeats and renews every lease.heartbeat_seconds 30, far inside the ttl, so a service restart of a few minutes never expires a live run's lease (T06 renews at a third or sooner; sooner is safe); the dead-launcher bound is N-12's 3 x 30 s = 90 s, not the ttl. One value, one key: N-07, N-12, N-15 and the seat contract read lease.heartbeat_seconds. The stall bound of N-12 is read from the same config so the two never disagree.
mechanism.liveness: A lease is never stolen while liveness is unknown: the only way a held key frees is Release by its token or expiry by the clock. No probe, no screen read, no model opinion (V08, K04).

start.rule: Nothing starts by an agent typing. Claim runs when N-07's tick finds a ticket.ready with no live lease; Sweep runs on every stall tick from N-06; Renew and Release are calls the seat launcher (N-15) makes as code around the one-shot run.
start.step: At service start, after the store opens, Recover: every lease row with released_at null and expires_at before now is swept as in step 4; every row with expires_at after now is left alone, because its holder may still be alive (a run that survived the service restart keeps its lease and its token).
The caps table is loaded from config; a missing key is exit 3 naming the key (SPEC-16 l-config, kept).
lease.recovered 100 is appended once with the counts swept and kept.

wait.name: claim-put
wait.fallback: 503 from the store; Claim retries 3 times with the same idempotency key; then N-07 treats the ticket as not dispatched this tick and tries next tick

wait.name: heartbeat
wait.fallback: Sweep expires the lease; lease.expired 500; N-12 kills, N-11 retries

wait.name: sweep
wait.timeout: stall.tick_seconds 15; a sweep older than 3 ticks is reported by N-06 health as tick.missed
wait.fallback: the next tick sweeps; a missed sweep delays expiry, never loses it

wait.name: cap
wait.timeout: none held here: a 429 returns at once
wait.fallback: N-07 re-evaluates every tick (level-triggered); nothing blocks on a cap

wait.name: hold
wait.timeout: none held here: a 423 hold returns at once
wait.fallback: N-07 re-evaluates every tick; the owner clears the hold through the Controls screen (N-42) and N-29

retries.rule: Every automated step retries up to 3 times, then recovers and reports.
retries.step: A store 503 or 409 on the counter row is retried 3 times with a fresh read and 1, 2, 4 s backoff; the fourth failure appends lease.failed 500 with the reason and N-07 leaves the ticket for the next tick; three lease.failed on one key in ten minutes is an owner-acts code through N-28.
The holder's renew retries 3 times inside N-15 with the same token; a renew that fails three times is not fatal by itself: the lease still has up to two heartbeat intervals before expiry.
A release that fails 3 times is left to the sweep: the lease expires by time and lease.expired carries the seat.result id that tried to release, so the record is evidence, not a lost release.
A sweep transaction failing is retried next tick; the per-key transaction means one bad row cannot stop the others.

many-agents.reading: N seats read their own lease by key through the ctl CLI; the token travels in the seat bundle (N-13) and the launcher's environment, never in a file two seats share.
many-agents.working: Twenty seats on twenty tickets hold twenty leases; the store serializes every claim; a seat never sees another seat's token.
many-agents.collision: N-07 on two ticks, or a recovered claim plus a live one, both Claim ticket:worker:1: the store's compare-and-swap on the lease row admits one; the other reads 423 held with the holder and expiry, and N-07 does not dispatch twice (level-triggered compare of open work with live runs, T02).

Attempt 1 went silent, the sweep expired it, N-11 cut attempt 2, N-02 granted a larger token; attempt 1 wakes and writes: its token is stale, every Put is 412, every renew is 412; it can only end with a seat.result the launcher records as blocked with reason stale, which N-11 ignores because attempt 2 is live (fencing, T06; the Optio lesson in S03 section 8 item 3).

Release and Sweep race on an expiring lease: both are transactions on the same row; whichever commits first wins; the loser's UPDATE affects zero rows and is logged; the outcome is either released (ticket progresses) or expired (N-11 retries), and N-11 reads the ticket's phase entity to tell which, so no attempt is lost or doubled.
Two claims for the last cap slot in one tick: the counting and the insert are one transaction behind the single writer, so exactly one gets 201 and the other 429.
The service restarts while a seat runs: Recover keeps every unexpired lease, the seat's token stays valid, its next heartbeat renews as if nothing happened.
many-agents.test: Two claimants per key over 100 keys, 1000 rounds, with a fake clock stepping past ttl in the middle: exactly one grant per generation, tokens strictly increasing across all keys, no Put with a stale token accepted.

path.cleanup: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-leases.sh: --dry-run lists released or expired lease rows older than lease.keep_days 30; --apply deletes them; never a live row

state-paths.rule: No other path. A lease is a row, never a file; the lease file of herdr/config/leases.json and the treehouse slot lease are retired by N-14's volume and N-49.

Do nothing by hand: the sweep expires it within ttl and N-12 kills it; the Alerts screen shows the stall. A hand release is break glass only.
Edit scheduler/config/scheduler.json through a ticket; `scheduler ctl reload` applies the tables; a running lease keeps its old expiry.
